Subject: [Architect Bridge] RSVP routing, late-snooze plan & tracking links

Team —

We need a quick alignment on the Architect Bridge webinar invite flow so we can lock the send tomorrow. High-level asks:

- Confirm final invite copy (below) and sponsor language from CloudFoundry.
- Approve target lists & routing rules (engineers vs. architects vs. platform leads).
- Provide tracking link matrix (HubSpot query params + fallback links for partner channels).
- Decide on a late-snooze rule for RSVP reminders (I propose a 72-hour snooze for opens w/o click).

Draft invite copy (subject + preview + body snippet):
Subject: Architect Bridge — Hands-on low-latency inference for platform teams
Preview: Live demo + routing tips for scaling inference in production — RSVP to reserve a lab seat
Body intro: Join Redwood engineers and CloudFoundry architects for a 45-min hands-on session covering compiler-level optimizations, batching patterns, and routing strategies that keep 99th-percentile latency predictable. Seats limited — register to reserve a lab environment.

Routing rules (initial proposal):
- Tier A (Platform Architects, infra leads): send from marissa_cole; include lab access note and priority RSVP link.
- Tier B (Engineers, SRE): send from aditya_rao; include quickstart checklist + general RSVP link.
- Partner-sourced leads: send via partners@cloudpartner.com with partner UTM and fallback to partner landing page.

Tracking link matrix: please populate HubSpot params: utm_source=redwood; utm_medium=email; utm_campaign=architect_bridge_2028; partner_id=cloudfoundry (for partner list). For partner emails we need a fallback link that doesn't rely on our shortener (in case of click-blocking).

I attached the hero banner and the audience CSV for reference. Marissa/Karthik — can you each take ownership of copy + segmentation by EOD? Stephanie, can you prep the HubSpot link set and a CDN fallback?

Thanks,
Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Growth & Events, Redwood Inference

Looks good — small edits inline.

Copy tweaks (suggested):
- Subject: change to "Architect Bridge — Hands-on: keep 99th P-tail latency under control" (shorter preview).
- Swap "lab environment" to "sandbox lab" to set expectations.
- Include one-sentence bullet on data handling (important for partner signoff).

Segmentation notes:
- Tier A: filter by title contains (Architect, Principal, Platform) + recent infra event attendance. Recommend ~1.8k recipients.
- Tier B: Engineered list is broader — recommend a 4k seed but stagger sends over 3 waves to avoid queueing latency in our dedicated pool.

Late-snooze: agree with 72 hours. Also recommend a 24-hour final reminder to only Tier A.

I'll update the CSV and push a version to the Drive folder.

-Marissa

Thanks — quick notes from ops side: 

- Stagger windows: send Tier B in 3 waves (08:00, 12:00, 16:00 PT) across two days to smooth GPU reservation spikes.
- RSVP capacity: the lab has 80 concurrent seats; use a soft cap at 70 and a waitlist with auto-promote rules (promote when cancellations drop below 60).
- Tracking: include a short numeric token in the query (eg. partner_token=CF123) so CloudFoundry can reconcile clicks against their leads.

On the fallback link: do both — CDN-hosted landing + partner-hosted landing where partner_url param is present. That way partners can keep a copy in their CRM if our shortener is blocked.

I'll add the wave schedule to the Drive spreadsheet and flag TTLs for promo links.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Growth Ops (campaigns), Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
